summary:
# Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an educational space-exploration simulation designed to introduce students, especially those aged 8–14, to the challenges of living and working beyond Earth.
The project allows users to explore the concept of establishing a research outpost on the Moon or Mars and understand the importance of resources, infrastructure, and survival systems in space.
### Problem Statement
Space exploration involves complex challenges such as limited water, oxygen and energy, extreme environmental conditions, and the need for safe habitats. These concepts can be difficult for young learners to understand through textbooks alone.
### Proposed Solution
The project presents these challenges through an interactive, game-inspired mission experience. Users are introduced to planetary environments, mission briefings, resource management concepts, and the infrastructure needed to support a future space outpost.
### Key Features in the Current Prototype- Moon and Mars mission concepts.- Mission briefing interface.- 3D planetary environment.- Space-outpost construction concepts.- Resource indicators for oxygen, water, food, and energy.- Camera viewing options.

Current Development Status
This is an early-stage working prototype. The main interface and initial simulation elements have been developed. Some navigation, interaction, and gameplay features remain incomplete and require further development and testing.
details:
I used ChatGPT and AI-assisted development tools during the project development process.

They helped me brainstorm the project concept, organize features, plan the user interface, understand Three.js, generate and improve code, and troubleshoot development issues.

I reviewed the suggestions and adapted them to my project requirements. AI tools were used as development assistance, while the project idea, feature selection, and final decisions were guided by my own understanding and objectives.
